jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-5947-tongass-national-forest-alaska.txt and jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5947.txt. The first command excludes home sites from the Tongass NF 'and restored to entry under the applicable public land laws'. Near the end there is a second operative act: 'And it is further ordered that Executive Order No. 5856, of June 11, 1932, excluding certain lands from the said national forest, be, and it is hereby, revoked in so far as it affects the tract ..., and that such tract shall remain part of the national forest and subject to the laws applicable to lands so situated'. The clause begins at character 16,098 (app text) or 17,627 (OFR text) of the whitespace-collapsed text, past the engine's 12,000-character window, so B08's outlier test ('remain part of', a revocation in part, and a forest retention) never saw it. The order therefore does two things: a spent exclusion, and a partial revocation of EO 5856 that keeps land in the forest. B08's single-exclusion description is false.
correct_lead: Doctrine treatment of a retention clause, as with EOs 4737 and 4055, points to B15 open (forest_designation_persists_pending_record) with the EO 5856 partial revocation disclosed. A no lead (TERM, 1932-11-16) holds only if the owner rules that both acts were spent on issue.
